items.description_en: Fire spread through the southern city streets to Baynard's Castle and began taking hold of St. Paul's, assisted by its scaffolds.
items.quote: saw the whole south part of the city burning from Cheapside to the Thames, and all along Cornhill (for it likewise kindled back against the wind as well as forward), Tower street, Fenchurch street, Gracious street, and so along to Baynard's Castle, and was now taking hold of St. Paul's church, to which the scaffolds contributed exceedingly.

items.description_en: Goods floated on the Thames, barges and boats carried salvaged property, and carts carried belongings into fields where tents were being erected.
items.quote: Here, we saw the Thames covered with goods floating, all the barges and boats laden with what some had time and courage to save, as, on the other side, the carts, etc., carrying out to the fields, which for many miles were strewn with movables of all sorts, and tents erecting to shelter both people and what goods they could get away.

items.description_en: Stones flew from St. Paul's, molten lead streamed down the streets, pavements glowed red, and demolition blocked the passages.
items.quote: the stones of Paul's flew like grenados, the melting lead running down the streets in a stream, and the very pavements glowing with fiery redness, so as no horse, nor man, was able to tread on them, and the demolition had stopped all the passages

items.description_en: People persisted in fighting the fire and blew up many houses to create gaps.
items.quote: It also broke out again in the temple; but the courage of the multitude persisting, and many houses being blown up, such gaps and desolations were soon made, as, with the former three days' consumption, the back fire did not so vehemently urge upon the rest as formerly.

items.description_en: Displaced inhabitants sheltered in tents, huts, and hovels, and many had no clothing or necessary household goods.
items.quote: The poor inhabitants were dispersed about St. George's Fields, and Moorfields, as far as Highgate, and several miles in circle, some under tents, some under miserable huts and hovels, many without a rag, or any necessary utensils, bed or board

items.description_en: The King and Duke worked in person and commanded, rewarded, or encouraged workmen.
items.quote: It is not indeed imaginable how extraordinary the vigilance and activity of the King and the Duke was, even laboring in person, and being present to command, order, reward, or encourage workmen

items.description_en: St. Paul's portico was broken apart, with large stones split and only its inscribed architrave remaining entire.
items.quote: that beautiful portico (for structure comparable to any in Europe, as not long before repaired by the late King) now rent in pieces, flakes of large stones split asunder, and nothing remaining entire but the inscription in the architrave showing by whom it was built, which had not one letter of it defaced!

items.description_en: Ruined fountains retained boiling water, while underground cellars, wells, and former warehouses continued burning with dark smoke.
items.quote: the fountains dried up and ruined, while the very waters remained boiling; the voragos of subterranean cellars, wells, and dungeons, formerly warehouses, still burning in stench and dark clouds of smoke

items.description_en: Towards Islington and Highgate, 200,000 people of all ranks lay dispersed beside heaps of salvaged possessions.
items.quote: I then went towards Islington and Highgate, where one might have seen 200,000 people of all ranks and degrees dispersed, and lying along by their heaps of what they could save from the fire, deploring their loss

items.description_en: Alarmed people abandoned their goods, seized weapons, and attacked people of the suspected nations before soldiers and guards sent them back into the fields under watch.
items.quote: This report did so terrify, that on a sudden there was such an uproar and tumult that they ran from their goods, and, taking what weapons they could come at, they could not be stopped from falling on some of those nations whom they casually met, without sense or reason. The clamor and peril grew so excessive, that it made the whole Court amazed, and they did with infinite pains and great difficulty, reduce and appease the people, sending troops of soldiers and guards, to cause them to retire into the fields again, where they were watched all this night.

items.description_en: People threw goods into the river or loaded lighters, then escaped burning houses by boats or waterside stairs.
items.quote: Everybody endeavouring to remove their goods, and flinging into the river or bringing them into lighters that layoff; poor people staying in their houses as long as till the very fire touched them, and then running into boats, or clambering from one pair of stairs by the water-side to another.

items.description_en: People carried goods away on their backs and in carts, while sick people were carried away in beds.
items.quote: every creature coming away loaden with goods to save, and here and there sicke people carried away in beds. Extraordinary good goods carried in carts and on backs.

items.description_en: The exhausted Lord Mayor wore a handkerchief around his neck in Canningstreet.
items.quote: At last met my Lord Mayor in Canningstreet, like a man spent, with a handkercher about his neck.

items.description_en: Thames-street had closely packed houses containing pitch and tar, and warehouses containing oil, wine, and brandy.
items.quote: The houses, too, so very thick thereabouts, and full of matter for burning, as pitch and tarr, in Thames-street; and warehouses of oyle, and wines, and brandy, and other things.

items.description_en: The streets were crowded with people, horses, and goods-laden carts nearly running over one another.
items.quote: the streets full of nothing but people and horses and carts loaden with goods, ready to run over one another, and, removing goods from one burned house to another.

items.description_en: The river was full of boats and lighters loading goods, with possessions floating in the water and virginals commonly among the household cargoes.
items.quote: River full of lighters and boats taking in goods, and good goods swimming in the water, and only I observed that hardly one lighter or boat in three that had the goods of a house in, but there was a pair of Virginalls

items.description_en: Pepys rode in a cart wearing his nightgown.
items.quote: Which I did riding myself in my night-gowne in the cart

items.description_en: Tower Hill was full of people's goods, and the crowd prevented passage through the postern.
items.quote: we did carry them (myself some) over Tower Hill, which was by this time full of people's goods, bringing their goods thither; and down to the lighter, which lay at next quay, above the Tower Docke. And here was my neighbour's wife, Mrs.-------,with her pretty child, and some few of her things, which I did willingly give way to be saved with mine; but there was no passing with any thing through the postern, the crowd was so great.

items.description_en: The Duke of York rode through the City with his guard to maintain order.
items.quote: did ride with his guard up and down the City, to keep all quiet

items.description_en: People worked with trays, dishes, and shovels scattered in Tower-street's gutters as fire advanced along both sides of the narrow street.
items.quote: his trayes, and dishes, shovells, &c., were flung all along Tower-street in the kennels, and people working therewith from one end to the other; the fire coming on in that narrow streete, on both sides, with infinite fury.
